Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

rear verb

bring up children or young animals

also bring up, raise (a child), raise a family, be brought up, rear animals, nurture, foster, raise (crops, animals)

classical

Cic. Lael. 75 (Lewis & Short)
Varr. in Non. 447.33: ēducit obstetrīx, ēducat nūtrīx, īnstituit paedagōgus, docet magister (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 166

ēducō, ēducāre, ēducāvī, ēducātum

verb, first conjugation

bring up, rear, educate

The whole upbringing of a child, body and mind. Not to be confused with ēdūcō, ēdūcere (long ū, third conjugation), “lead out”, which can also mean rear (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • alō, alere, aluī, altum (alitum) — nourish, feed, raise

    conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 3.4.36 (Lewis & Short, s.v. ēducō): Athēnīs nātus altusque ēducātusque Atticīs

    To feed and keep a child or an animal; nātus altusque, born and bred. Also of keeping animals (canēs alere).

Examples

  • vidēn tū puerum hunc … quem tam humilī cultū ēducāmus?

    do you see this boy, whom we are bringing up in such a humble way?Liv. 1.39.3

  • in hujus sinū indulgentiāque ēducātus per omnem honestārum artium cultum pueritiam adulēscentiamque trānsēgit

    brought up in her lap and in her care, he spent his boyhood and youth in the study of every liberal artTac. Agr. 4.2

See also education, parents, child.
